title: Strict convexity of the level-two Gamma-ratio curve
statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be the Euler Gamma function. For each $x>0$, let $h(x)>0$ be the unique solution of
$$\frac{\Gamma(h(x))\Gamma(h(x)+2x)}{\Gamma(h(x)+x)^2}=2.$$
Is $h$ strictly convex on the whole interval $(0,\infty)$? Explicitly, for distinct $x_0,x_1>0$ and $0<\lambda<1$, must
$$h(\lambda x_0+(1-\lambda)x_1)<\lambda h(x_0)+(1-\lambda)h(x_1)?$$
This is the question in Garrappa–Gerhold–Popolizio–Simon, Remark 16(a), with $h$ defined in Lemma 15. The source establishes strict convexity on $[1,\infty)$. This record concerns the shape of that Gamma-ratio curve, not the separate complete-Bernstein-function and reverse Mittag–Leffler inequality conjectures.
references:
R. Garrappa, S. Gerhold, M. Popolizio and T. Simon, On some inequalities for the two-parameter Mittag–Leffler function in the complex plane, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 551 (2025), 129588. Lemma 15 and Remark 16(a). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmaa.2025.129588
https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11852v4
label: proof

title: The exact dyadic denominator law in shifted Jacobi parameters
statement:
Let $u=\alpha^2-\tfrac14$ and $v=\beta^2-\tfrac14$ be independent indeterminates. Following Area's formal Definition 2.1, put
$$P_\ell(z)=\prod_{0\le j<\ell}(z-j(j+1)),\qquad
C_s(\xi,\eta)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{s}\frac{P_\ell(u)P_{s-\ell}(v)}{\ell!(s-\ell)!}\xi^\ell\eta^{s-\ell}.$$
In the formal $Z^{-1}$-adic ring define
$$F(Z)=\sum_{s\ge0}C_s(\xi,\eta)\prod_{j=1}^{s}(Z-j)^{-1},\qquad
L_n(\xi,\eta)=[Z^{-n}]\log F(Z),$$
and
$$\kappa_r(u,v)=2^{-(2r-1)}\operatorname{Im}L_{2r-1}\!\left(\frac{1+i}{2},\frac{1-i}{2}\right).$$
Empty products are one; coefficient extraction is finite at each order, and $u,v$ are treated as real formal variables.

**Shifted-parameter question (Remark 3.8).** For every integer $r\ge1$, is the maximum dyadic denominator exponent among the rational coefficients of $\kappa_r(u,v)$ exactly
$$2r+\nu_2((r-1)!)?$$
For a nonzero rational coefficient $c$, this exponent is $\max(0,-\nu_2(c))$; zero imposes no denominator. Odd denominator factors are allowed. This is distinct from the original-variable law in $\alpha^2,\beta^2$, whose exponent is $3r-1+\nu_2((r-1)!)$. No analytic all-order phase-identification assertion is part of this formal question.
references:
I. Area, Dyadic denominator bounds and a transfer principle for the phase constants of Jacobi zeros, arXiv:2608.23006v2, Definition 2.1, equations (6)–(7), and Remark 3.8. https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23006v2
For the distinct original-variable law: I. Area, The ultraspherical background of the Jacobi phase expansion, in closed form, arXiv:2609.29531v2. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29531v2
label: proof

title: Two nested power-mean inequalities for the logarithm–arctangent mean
statement:
For $a,b>0$, define $M(a,a)=a$ and, when $a\ne b$,
$$M(a,b)=\frac{b-a}{\sqrt2\,\arctan((\log b-\log a)/\sqrt2)}.$$
For $r\ne0$ let $B_r(a,b)=((a^r+b^r)/2)^{1/r}$. Put $d=\sqrt{17}$, $\alpha=(5+d)/2$, and $\beta=(5-d)/2$.

**Displayed inequalities in Conjecture 37.** For all distinct positive $a,b$, do both inequalities hold?
$$M(a,b)<B_d\!\left(M(a,B_\beta(a,b)),M(B_\beta(a,b),b)\right),$$
$$M(a,b)<B_{-d}\!\left(M(a,B_\alpha(a,b)),M(B_\alpha(a,b),b)\right).$$
This is the two-branch displayed claim of Mihoković–Raïssouli, published Conjecture 37 (earlier arXiv Conjecture 4.7), with their mean $M_2$. The diagonal gives equality. The separate between-means condition used in the source's terminology “super-stabilizable” is not included in this record.
references:
L. Mihoković and M. Raïssouli, Results on comparison and sub/super-stabilizability of some new means, Applicable Analysis and Discrete Mathematics 20(1) (2026), 1–23; equation (5), p. 4, and Conjecture 37, p. 21. https://doi.org/10.2298/AADM240618001M
https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13618v2
label: proof

title: Positivity of real H-eigenvalues for reflected order-four Steiner distance tensors
statement:
Let $T$ be a finite tree on $n\ge2$ vertices. For an ordered quadruple of vertices, including repeated terminals, let $M_{ijkl}$ be the minimum number of edges in a connected subgraph containing those terminals. Let $J$ be the all-ones $n\times n$ matrix and $A=2J/n-I$. Reflect the last slot:
$$(C_1)_{ijkl}=\sum_h M_{ijkh}A_{hl}.$$
Using the first-free-index H-eigenvalue convention, a real H-eigenpair is a real number $\lambda$ and a nonzero vector $x\in\mathbb R^n$ such that
$$\sum_{j,k,l}(C_1)_{ijkl}x_jx_kx_l=\lambda x_i^3\quad\text{for every }i.$$

**Positivity question.** Must every such real H-eigenvalue be positive for every tree $T$?

This is the order-four case of the reflected-tensor positivity question on pp. 9–10 of Cooper–Du. The reflection need not leave a fully symmetric tensor, so the coordinate convention is explicit. This question is separate from the hyperdeterminant-sign conjecture and from positivity results for $C_1+C_3$.
references:
J. Cooper and Z. Du, Determinants of Steiner Distance Hypermatrices, arXiv:2505.10501v1 (2025), Theorem 2.1 and pp. 9–10. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10501v1
L. Qi, Eigenvalues of a real supersymmetric tensor, J. Symbolic Comput. 40 (2005), 1302–1324. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsc.2005.05.007
label: counterexample

title: The quadratic universal-container formula for fixed polyominoes
statement:
Identify square lattice cells with points of $\mathbb Z^2$, adjacent when their Manhattan distance is one. A polyomino is a finite nonempty edge-connected set of cells. Let $a(n)$ be the least cardinality of a finite connected container $C\subset\mathbb Z^2$ such that every $n$-cell polyomino $P$ admits an integer translation $t$ with $P+t\subseteq C$.

Orientations are fixed: every rotated or reflected shape is an input in its own right, and a placement allows translation only. Holes are permitted.

**Formula proposed in OEIS A395495.** Is
$$a(n)=\frac{n^2-n+6}{2}\qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge4?$$
This record concerns that universal formula, not a claim of optimality for any smaller proposed container.
references: Peter Exley, OEIS A395495, proposed formula for the translation-only universal-container problem, n ≥ 4. https://oeis.org/A395495
label: counterexample

title: A subunit Rényi threshold for exponential-maximal iid entropy increments
statement:
For a probability density $f$ on $\mathbb R$ and $0<p<1$, define
$$h_p(f)=\frac{\log\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)^p\,dx}{1-p},\qquad
(f*f)(s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(t)f(s-t)\,dt,\qquad
\Delta_p(f)=h_p(f*f)-h_p(f),$$
whenever the two power integrals are finite and strictly positive. Thus $\Delta_p(f)$ is the Rényi entropy increment of the sum of two independent random variables with density $f$. Let $e(x)=e^{-x}\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}(x)$.

**Subunit threshold question.** Does there exist $p_0\in(0,1)$ such that for every $p_0<p<1$ and every log-concave probability density $f$ with the required finite positive moments,
$$\Delta_p(f)\le\Delta_p(e)?$$
This is the one-dimensional necessary consequence of the proposed exponential-maximizer branch in the unnumbered paragraph after (1.2), p. 2, of Fu–Li. It is distinct from the numbered Shannon conjecture ($p=1$), and does not ask about the proposed cube-uniform branch below the threshold.
references: Fu–Li, A reverse entropy power inequality for iid log-concave random variables, arXiv:2510.09206v3, p. 2, unnumbered paragraph after (1.2). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09206v3
label: counterexample
